title: Outreach Voice Template v2
summary: Upgraded outreach template with zero-risk offer framework and social proof.
content:
Outreach Voice Template v2

Upgraded by Jacob. 2026-03-12. Builds on Patrik's original voice template with zero-risk offer framework, social proof, and subject line variants.

What changed from v1:

  • Added zero-risk offer CTA (replaces "talk shop" with a concrete free offer)
  • Added one line of casual social proof (no stats, no case studies)
  • 3 subject line variants for A/B testing
  • All voice rules from v1 still apply exactly as written

Subject Line Variants

Variant A (Original): really impressed by [Company Name] work Variant B: quick question about [Company Name] Variant C: idea for [Company Name]

Use Variant A as the control. Test B and C in equal splits across batches. If the company name is long (3+ words), shorten or rephrase so it reads natural. Same rule as v1.

The Email (Base Template v2)

{First name}, I came across [Company Name] the other day and [specific observation about their work]. [Personalized detail or compliment].

We've been working with a contractor here in the Valley on their online presence and it's been going really well. I actually had a couple ideas that could work for you guys too.

No strings, no pitch. Want me to send over a quick video with what I had in mind?

{DEFAULT GMAIL SIGNATURE}

Template Breakdown

Paragraph 1: The Opener (same energy as v1)

  • Opens with their first name. Always.
  • References something SPECIFIC about their business. Not "your stuff looks solid." What looks solid? A project, a review, a photo from their site, something real.
  • One personalized detail. A memory, an observation, a compliment that couldn't be copy-pasted to someone else.

Paragraph 2: Social Proof + Bridge

  • One casual line establishing that AOM works with people like them.
  • Bridges into "I had ideas for you too." Natural transition from proof to offer.

Paragraph 3: The Zero-Risk Offer (NEW)

  • This is the upgrade. Instead of "talk shop sometime," we offer something free and specific.
  • "No strings, no pitch" = the risk reversal. They get value even if they never hire AOM.
  • "Quick video with what I had in mind" = the deliverable. Patrik records a 60-90 second personalized Loom or voice note with actual ideas for their business.
  • The CTA is now "want me to send you something?" instead of "call me if you want." Way easier to say yes to.

Social Proof Lines (Rotate These)

Use ONE per email. Never the same line twice in a batch. All are vague enough to reuse, specific enough to be real.

  1. "We've been working with a contractor here in the Valley on their online presence and it's been going really well."
  2. "Been working with a couple contractors in Phoenix on getting their work out there."
  3. "We just wrapped a brand build for a mechanical company out here and it came out solid."
  4. "I've been helping some companies in the trades get their work in front of more people."
  5. "We recently helped a Phoenix contractor completely redo how they show up online."

Social Proof Rules

  • One line. Max. Never a paragraph.
  • No company names. No stats. No "3x engagement." No testimonials.
  • It should sound like something Patrik would casually mention in conversation, not a pitch deck.
  • If it doesn't fit the email naturally, leave it out. Not every email needs it.

Zero-Risk Offer Variants

The base offer is a personalized video (Loom or voice note). But the offer can flex based on the prospect:

Default (most emails): "Want me to send over a quick video with what I had in mind?"

For companies with upcoming events: "If you guys have any events or jobsite tours coming up, I'd love to come film one. No charge. You'd get the content either way."

For high-value targets (use sparingly): "I actually mocked up a quick idea for a post that could work for [Company Name]. No strings. Want me to send it over?"

Zero-Risk Offer Rules

  • The offer must be FREE. No catches, no "free consultation" (that's a sales call in disguise).
  • The prospect gets something useful even if they never respond again.
  • Keep it casual. "Want me to send it over?" not "Would you be interested in receiving a complimentary audit?"
  • Only promise what AOM can actually deliver. Patrik records a quick Loom (5 min of his time), not a full production.

AI Systems Mention (Unchanged from v1)

Same rules. ~1 out of 5 emails. Casual, almost uncertain. Never a pitch. If it doesn't fit, leave it out.

Voice Rules (Carried from v1, Still Active)

  • EVERY email MUST open with the prospect's first name.
  • This is a real person reaching out because he noticed something. Not a pitch.
  • No case studies. No stats. No clever hooks or subject line tricks.
  • No assumptions about what they need or what's wrong.
  • "I can tell you guys care about your work" = the energy. Genuine respect, not flattery.
  • Keep it short. If it feels like a brochure, delete and start over.
  • Default Gmail signature on every email. No custom sign-offs.
  • Email 1 is not trying to sell anything. It's opening a door.
  • DO NOT repeat the same words/phrases across emails.
  • Every email must feel like it was written for that one person.
  • Adapt the pitch line to the industry.

Personalization (Unchanged, Still Mandatory)

  • Research their actual business. Reference specific projects, locations, specialties.
  • Add a personal touch when possible.
  • Vary the opening. Vary the compliment. Never repeat the same phrase across a batch.
  • If you can't find something specific, dig harder. The template is a last resort, not the default.

Multi-Touch Sequence (Updated)

  • Email 1: This v2 template (zero-risk offer)
  • Email 2 (5 days): Follow up on the offer. "Hey {First name}, just wanted to make sure that video idea didn't get buried. Still happy to send it over if you're interested." Or a different angle referencing something they posted.
  • Email 3 (7 days): Even shorter. "Still thinking about what you guys are building. Let me know if you ever want to grab coffee."
  • Touches 4+: LinkedIn, Instagram follow, DM. Just being present.

Same energy every time. Never escalate the pressure.

What v2 Replaces

v2 replaces v1 as the active template ONLY after Patrik approves. Until then, v1 remains the source of truth. This file exists for review and comparison.
